# 1 Enoch Chapter 96 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** Hold on, you righteous ones — have hope! The sinners will suddenly vanish right before your eyes, and you will have power over them, exactly as you have longed for.

**2** When the day of the sinners' tribulation arrives, your children will rise up and soar like eagles — higher than the vultures, your nest will sit. You will climb into the crevices of the earth, the clefts of the rock, sheltering there like rock hyraxes away from the unrighteous, while wailing creatures mourn over you.

**3** Don't be afraid, you who have suffered — healing is your inheritance. A brilliant light will shine on you, and from heaven you will hear the voice saying: "Rest."

**4** Woe to you, sinners — your wealth makes you look like righteous people. But your hearts are witnesses against you. They know what you are. And that knowledge will stand as a permanent record of your evil deeds.

**5** Woe to you who eat the finest grain and drink wine by the bowlful while grinding down the poor with your power.

**6** Woe to you who drink from every fountain — you will be suddenly consumed, you will dry up and wither, because you have abandoned the fountain of life.

**7** Woe to you who build your lives on injustice, deception, and contempt for God — these things will stand as your permanent indictment.

**8** Woe to you, the powerful, who crush the righteous with your strength — your day of destruction is coming. And when that day arrives, the righteous will be living their best days, right in the middle of your judgment.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The contrast in v. 8 is devastating in its irony: the day of the oppressors' judgment is simultaneously described as the "many good days" of the righteous. The Enochic tradition believes deeply in eschatological reversal. V. 2's strange imagery — the righteous as rock hyraxes hiding from their hunters — captures a community genuinely in hiding, genuinely afraid. V. 6's "fountain of life" is the clearest echo of Jeremiah in the Epistle.*
